summary:
Celestia is a free, browser and mobile space-exploration game that teaches NASA mission design through play. Players explore the Moon and all seven other planets. They scan landmarks, drill for resources, collect materials, and fly a rocket whose trips follow real mission concepts: launch windows, delta-v, and trajectory correction. Every fact is labeled Fact, Hypothesis, or Game fiction. It makes space science hands-on and honest for students.
Detailed Description:
Celestia is a 2D pixel-art adventure with a cabin you can walk around. The cabin has a moving crew, a galley, and arcade games. Each world has a NASA info console, 3 landmarks, rare materials, supply crates, and drillable ore. Mini-games teach the four mission segments, Mission Design Lab study levels, Concept Maturity Levels, and GMAT-style flight checks, and there's a 3D mission-orbit viewer. A Space Apps NPC teaches the Space Apps steps. It's built with plain HTML, JavaScript, and Canvas. It's packaged as a PWA and an Android APK, and works offline.
NASA Data:
NASA public facts and concepts: Apollo 11, the LCROSS water discovery, Voyager, Curiosity, Hubble, JWST, the Mission Design Lab, JPL Concept Maturity Levels, and the open-source GMAT trajectory software.
Space Agency Partner & Other Data:
No external datasets are used. Code, art, and text are original.
details:
Celestia is a free educational space-exploration game for browsers and phones. The player is an astronaut who explores the Moon and all seven other planets, collecting rare materials that power "Earth's energy reserve". Along the way, players learn how real space missions are designed. Every piece of information is labeled Fact, Hypothesis, or Game fiction, so students always know what is real science and what is gameplay.

How it works:

- NASA lobby: A guide teaches NASA basics (Apollo 11, Voyager, Curiosity, Hubble, JWST) and issues a launch pass after a short quiz.

- Rocket cabin: The player walks around a living cabin with a moving crew, a galley, and an arcade. The Navigation console picks the destination, the Engine bay upgrades the rocket, and the Mission Viz shows the trajectory in 3D.

- Flight: Each trip follows real mission concepts. Players choose the right mission scenario, check the launch window, and perform a correction burn, in the style of NASA's GMAT software. Delta-v decides which worlds are reachable.

- Planets: Each world has an info console with NASA facts, three landmarks to scan, supply crates, and a confirmed and a hypothetical material. The hypothetical one is unlocked with a quiz. Players can also drill for ore with a heat-management mini-game or pick up loose ore.

- Learning games: The crew and mini-games teach the four mission segments (launch, space, ground, user), the Mission Design Lab study levels, and Concept Maturity Levels.

- Space Apps: A character teaches the Space Apps steps and quizzes the player.

Benefits: It turns hard mission-design ideas into hands-on play, separates fact from theory, needs no account, and works offline on any phone or computer.

What we hope to achieve: Inspire students to see space exploration as something they can design, and introduce them to NASA's open tools and resources

Tools and technology: Plain HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and the Canvas API.
